channel.title: The Chronicle of Higher Education - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Chronicle of Higher Education (chronicle.com)

item.title: Assessment Is Ruining Teaching
item.description: In trying to routinize education, we're losing sight of what it can be at its best.By Andrew Davinack In trying to routinize education, we're losing sight of what it can be at its best.

item.title: What's Max Weber Doing in the Columbia Antisemitism Report?
item.description: The great sociologist knew that activism can be a threat to scholarship — and so can government. By Len Gutkin The great sociologist knew that activism can be a threat to scholarship — and so can government.

item.title: Oklahoma Is 'Phasing Out' Tenure. Will the Idea Catch On?
item.description: By Megan Zahneis A governor's executive order has left the state's professors with more questions than answers — and touched off concerns that tenure may be under threat nationwide.

item.title: Iowa, Kansas Consider Bills to Ban Race, Gender, Sexuality Content in Some College Courses
item.description: Explore where college diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts are under attack.By Chronicle StaffLegislators want to get rid of DEI offices, end diversity trainings, banish diversity statements, and censor how professors talk about race, gender, and sexuality in mandatory courses.

item.title: The Heritage Foundation Drove Trump's 2025 Higher-Ed Agenda. What's Its Plan for 2026?
item.description: By Rick Seltzer Accreditation is in the crosshairs. Adam Kissel, a visiting fellow and author of a new Heritage policy blueprint, explains why.

item.title: David Brooks: 'We're Part of the Problem'
item.description: David Brooks on the sins of the educated class, what Trump gets right, and why he's leaving 'The New York Times' for Yale University.By Evan Goldstein The New York Times columnist on the sins of the educated class, what Trump gets right, and why he's leaving the newspaper to take a new job at Yale University.

item.title: A Group of Deans Boycotted This Year's U.S. News Survey, and It Worked
item.description: By Francie Diep The publication is pausing its social-work graduate-school ranking in 2026. It will resume in 2027.

item.title: UCLA’s Head of Finance Alleged Years of Mismanagement. Days Later, He Was Fired.
item.description: By Dan Berrett The very public airing of financial difficulties at one of the nation's premier universities was unusual.

item.title: Daniel Diermeier Is Higher Ed's Most Divisive Figure. He's Fine With That.
item.description: Daniel Diermeier says reform will save the sector. His critics say he's exploiting its crisis.By Kate Hidalgo Bellows The Vanderbilt chancellor says reform will save the sector. His critics say he's promoting himself.

item.title: What Trump's Top Higher-Ed Official Has in Mind for College Accreditation
item.description: By Eric Kelderman In an interview, Nicholas Kent, the undersecretary of education, said the department was interested in "revolutionizing" the process.
